input.quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
input.rationale: The governing-law clause selects Nova Scotia/Canadian law with non-exclusive jurisdiction of the Nova Scotia courts. Nova Scotia is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), and non-exclusive venue leaves us exposed to suit in an unaccepted forum. No arbitration is required, so litigation-in-courts is already satisfied. We moved the clause to the preferred position (New York law, exclusive state and federal courts in New York County) with a minimal edit to the jurisdiction and forum words only, and flagged Delaware/California or England and Wales (London courts) as fallbacks.

proposal.summary: Replace Nova Scotia governing law and venue with New York law and exclusive New York County courts
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced Nova Scotia law and the non-exclusive Nova Scotia courts with New York law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, which is our accepted governing-law position. If New York is not workable, we can accept Delaware or California, or the laws of England and Wales with the courts of London.
